name: Next Step Board
version: v1.2 · 2026-11-18 · meeting notes into minutes (s23–s30) · store step: free · +2 steps: Make it mine (22 Nov)
verified: 2026-11-15 · Next Step Board v1.10 · 2026-10-11 · driven twice on a fresh test copy at phone width, all 20 app steps as written
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this app has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the app already shows your own information, you have opened your real app: go back to your list and tap this app's name again, rather than using a bookmark, your history, or an icon on your home screen. Starting in the wrong copy makes the early steps look broken when nothing is wrong.

The test copy mark is a small pill now, and it no longer covers the form's “Add it” button. You will set up the board, add a project of your own with its next step, mark it Waiting, give it a checklist, check that it stays put after a reload and with no internet, then turn a page of meeting notes into minutes with your own AI. A short setup may be offered after the welcome tour, four questions you answer by tapping. Unless a step tells you to try it, tap “No thanks, just open it”.

steps.do: Tap “skip the tour” (the small underlined words at the bottom right of the welcome card).
steps.see: The card now asks “How do you want to start?” with two big choices.
steps.tip: A green greeting strip may show at the top for a few seconds. Tap it to close it, or just wait.

steps.do: Tap “🧪 Keep the examples to play with”.
steps.see: The card closes. A small “✨ A new look” note appears near the bottom of the screen.

steps.do: Tap “Got it ✓” on that note.
steps.see: The note closes. You see “My Next Step Board” at the top and example cards below it, starting with “👋 Start here (delete me when you’re ready)”.

steps.do: Scroll down to the bottom of the board and tap “+ Add project”.
steps.see: A form called “+ Add a project” slides up, with boxes for Project name, Emoji, One line, The next step, and Who / how long.

steps.do: In the “Project name” box, type the example below.
steps.see: The name appears in the box.

steps.do: In the box under “The next step”, type the example below.
steps.type: Call the church about the hall
steps.see: The words appear in that box. “Who / how long?” already says “Me”.

steps.do: Tap “Add it”.
steps.see: The form closes and a short note says “Project added”. A new card “📁 Margaret O'Brien's retirement party” is on the board with NEXT STEP “Call the church about the hall”. At the bottom it now says “5 projects”.

steps.do: On your new card, tap “Status ▸”.
steps.see: The label on the card changes from ACTIVE to WAITING, and a short note says “Status: waiting”. The card moves down the board, below the other active cards.

steps.do: Scroll back to the top and tap “Waiting” in the row of buttons under the title.
steps.see: Only two cards show: “📚 Example: Bookkeeping catch-up” and your “Margaret O'Brien's retirement party” card. It says “5 projects” at the bottom (that counts the whole board).

steps.do: Tap “All” to see every card again.
steps.see: All five cards are back.

steps.do: On your new card, tap “No checklist yet ▾”, then type the example in the “add an item…” box.
steps.see: The checklist opens with an empty “add an item…” box and an “Add” button; your words are in the box.

steps.do: Tap “Add” next to that box.
steps.see: A short note says “Added”. The card now says “Checklist (1 open)” with “Book the caterer — Me” and a tick box.

steps.do: Tap the tick box next to “Book the caterer”.
steps.see: A note says the checklist is CLEAR (“🏁 … checklist CLEAR”). The checklist folds shut and the card says “Checklist (0 open) ▾”. Tap that to open it again: “Book the caterer” is crossed off.

steps.do: Pull the page down to reload it (or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: The board comes back. Your “Margaret O'Brien's retirement party” card is still there, still WAITING, and “Checklist (0 open) ▾” opens to show “Book the caterer” ticked off. The bottom still says “5 projects”.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode (swipe down from the top-right corner, tap ✈️). Then scroll to the bottom and tap “+ Add project”.
steps.see: A brown strip at the top says “No connection right now — the app still works and saves on this phone.” The “+ Add a project” form opens as before.

steps.do: Type the example in “Project name”, then tap “Add it”.
steps.see: “Project added” shows, and a new “📁 Fix the back door” card is on the board. The bottom says “6 projects”.

steps.do: Turn Airplane Mode off. Then tap “+ Add project” again and, without typing anything, tap “Add it”.
steps.see: The brown “No connection” strip goes away. Nothing is added: the form stays open and the “Project name” box is outlined, waiting for a name.

steps.do: Tap “Cancel” on the form.
steps.see: The form closes. Still “6 projects”.

steps.do: On the “Fix the back door” card, tap the red ✕ (right of “✏️ Card”). When the box asks “Delete "Fix the back door" and its checklist? (Backup first if unsure)”, tap OK.
steps.see: The card disappears, a note says “Deleted”, and the bottom says “5 projects”.

steps.do: Scroll to the very top and read the 👋 “Where you left off” box.
steps.see: It says “2 projects waiting” (the bookkeeping example and your party).

steps.do: Scroll to the bottom of the board and tap “📝 Turn meeting notes into minutes”.
steps.see: A sheet opens called “📝 Turn meeting notes into minutes”. It has a “Step 1 — your notes” box with a “✨ Ask my AI to write the minutes” button, and a “Step 2 — paste what your AI said” box under it.

steps.do: Tap the Step 1 box and type the example below.
steps.type: HOA board mtg Tue 11/18. Present Maria, Tom, Janet. Pool fence quote $4,200 approved. Annual meeting moves to Jan 14. Tom to call 3 paving companies by 12/1. Janet sends the fence deposit by 11/25.
steps.see: Your notes are in the box.

steps.do: Tap “✨ Ask my AI to write the minutes”. If it first asks “Which AI do you use?”, tap the one you use (Claude if you are not sure).
steps.see: A sheet shows the start of the question, with a small “see the words” link. Its big button says either “Send it →” or “Open Claude →” (or the name of the AI you picked).
steps.tip: Tap “see the words” if you are curious: it asks for the minutes and for the action items in a list the board can read. It never includes anything else from your board.

steps.do: Tap the big button. If it said “Send it →”, just wait. If it opened Claude (or ChatGPT), let it answer, copy the WHOLE answer, come back to Next Step Board, paste it into the “Paste the answer” box and tap “Use this answer”.
steps.see: A sheet called “📝 Your minutes” opens, with the minutes in a box: Meeting, Date, Attendees (Maria, Tom, Janet), Decisions (the $4,200 pool fence) and Action items. Below the box are “📋 Copy the minutes” and “🖨 Print the minutes”, then a ticked list of action items with who does each one.
steps.tip: The AI writes the words, so they will not match these exactly. What matters is that nothing in them is made up: no people, dates or decisions that were not in your notes. If something is made up, say so.

steps.do: Tap “📋 Copy the minutes”.
steps.see: The button changes to “Copied ✓”. (If you paste into Notes or a text message, the minutes are there.)

steps.do: Tap “🖨 Print the minutes”.
steps.see: A print preview opens showing only the minutes, headed “📝 Minutes”. No buttons and none of the board's cards are on the page. Close the preview without printing.

steps.do: Look at “Put them on” under the action items. Leave it on “＋ A new project” and tap the big button under it (it says “Add 2 action items and keep the minutes”, or another number if the AI found more).
steps.see: The sheet closes and a note says “📝 Minutes kept on …”. A new card with 📝 is on the board: its checklist holds the action items, each with its owner, and under it is “📝 Minutes (1) ▾”. The bottom says “6 projects”.

steps.do: On that new card, tap “📝 Minutes (1) ▾”, then tap the line with today's date that appears under it.
steps.see: The minutes open again, with “Kept” and today's date, and buttons “📋 Copy”, “🖨 Print” and “Remove these minutes”. Tap “✕ close”.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=nextstep&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=nextstep  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=nextstep&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to match what is being said, and when it points at something, that thing is really there. If a video talks about a button or a screen you did not see in this app, say so — that is a real fault and one of the most useful things you can find.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees before they buy: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find this app on its shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The price says Free, with an optional donation to Loving InDeed. That is right: nothing is sold, and nobody has to give. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit.

steps.do: Tap the ? button at the top right, then tap “Make it mine”. If it shows “Set it up now”, tap that and answer the four questions by tapping. (If you already answered them when the app first opened, tap “Answer them again”.)
steps.see: Four questions, one at a time, each answered with one tap. At the end it says “Done — that is yours now”. Say whether the questions made sense for this app, and whether any answer you wanted was missing.

steps.do: Tap ? then “Make it mine” again, then tap “✨ Make it mine — ask for something”. Ask for one report you would really want from this app, in your own words. Answer its questions.
steps.see: It asks you a few short questions, then builds a report. Tell us: did the questions make sense, and is the report something you would actually use? If it cannot make one, write down exactly what it said.
